The statement signals a sharp negative shock to real activity and financial conditions, but the policy mix—cutting the funds rate to the effective lower bound, launching large-scale Treasury and agency MBS purchases, expanded repos, discount-window easing, capital and liquidity buffer flexibility, and dollar swap lines—is aligned with the credit view literature showing that easing financial frictions lowers the external finance premium and prevents balance-sheet-driven amplification (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein; Gertler and Gilchrist; Oliner and Rudebusch). With market-based inflation compensation down and survey expectations little changed, the risk set includes disinflation/deflation; at the zero lower bound, balance-sheet tools help avoid a liquidity trap and support aggregate spending (Svensson; Romer and Romer; Sims and Zha). Consistent with the Friedman–Phelps natural-rate perspective, these measures support maximum employment without invoking a long-run inflation–unemployment trade-off. Net tone: still negative due to the immediate COVID-19 hit, but less so given decisive, literature-consistent stabilization tools.
